entries.title: An invitation against the feeling
entries.literal_meaning: Ill-feeling within, yet falsely saying, “Friend, sit, sit.” Provisional: exact କକରଣ is read through nearby noun sense2, not silently changed to the headword କକରଶ.
entries.explanation: The invitation repeats, but the line declares a contrary feeling within. The nearby noun definition supplies ill-feeling, not the separate bodily or fever senses. Our reading concerns words of welcome that conceal reluctance; it does not prove anyone’s hidden feelings in an actual encounter.
entries.meaning_odia: ବସିବାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଡାକ, ଅଥଚ ମନରେ ଅନ୍ୟ ଭାବ—ପଦଟି ଏହି ତଫାତ କହେ। ଉତ୍ସର କକରଣ ରୂପକୁ ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ଖରାପ ଭାବ ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ିବା ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ, ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଶବ୍ଦସଂଶୋଧନ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହା ଜ୍ୱରର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ସ୍ୱାଗତର କଥା ଅନିଚ୍ଛାକୁ ଲୁଚାଏ; କୌଣସି ପ୍ରକୃତ ସାକ୍ଷାତରେ ମନ କଥା ଜାଣିବାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମିଳେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Repeated welcome contrasts with the feeling the line describes.
entries.odia_summary: ବାରମ୍ବାର ଡାକ ସହ ପଦରେ କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା ମନର ଭାବ ମେଳେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ବନ୍ଧୁ ଅନିଚ୍ଛାରେ ଡାକିବା ବଦଳରେ ଆଉ ଦିନ ଦେଖାହେବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / An imagined friend suggests another day instead of offering an unwilling welcome. This alternative response is invented.
entries.cultural_context: One dictionary witness; exact quotation-word discrepancy remains unresolved. No medical reading or specified relationship beyond the address “friend”.
